comment: The FIFTH typecheck pass. Covers the two trees the other four leave completely unchecked: the `tests/` suite (minus `tests/react/`, which tsconfig.react.test.json already owns because it needs react-jsx) and the package tooling files (config/vite/*.ts and config/playwright/*.ts, both reached by the `config/**/*.ts` include; plus the package-root vitest.config.ts and vitest.shims.d.ts, reached by the non-recursive `*.ts`). No vite or playwright config remains at the package root: all 22 vite configs and all 14 playwright configs moved under config/ in the 2026-09-01 consolidation, which is why `config/**/*.ts` is load-bearing rather than decorative -- drop it and this pass keeps printing zero errors while reading 36 fewer files. Before this pass existed, `nx typecheck ui` read 548 of the 677 .ts/.tsx files in the package: tsconfig.json included only `src/**` (it now also includes `mcp/**`, less its `mcp/mcp` and `mcp/tests` excludes), tsconfig.react.json only `frameworks/**`, tsconfig.react.test.json only `tests/react/**`, tsconfig.mcp.json only `mcp/mcp/**` — so a type error anywhere else shipped green. Strictness is deliberately the same as tsconfig.json (strict + isolatedModules); the JSX config is Solid's, matching the suite. DO NOT relax these options to make the pass green — quarantine a file in `exclude` with a reason instead, so the gap stays visible. Every exclusion is audited by `node scripts/verify-quarantine.mjs`, which runs as part of `npm run typecheck`.
allowJsIs: A note on `allowJs`, because it looks like the kind of loosening the comment above forbids and is the opposite. tests/scripts/ imports two plain build scripts (scripts/_ts-helpers.mjs, scripts/run-storybook-tests.mjs). WITHOUT allowJs TypeScript will not read them, so under noImplicitAny each import is a TS7016 error and every function it brings in is `any` — the calls go unchecked. WITH it, TypeScript infers real signatures from the .mjs and the calls are checked; `checkJs` stays off, so the .mjs bodies are inferred from, not checked. Measured when it went in: it added exactly those 2 files to the program and nothing else (`include` names no JS extension, so only IMPORTED JavaScript is reachable), it cleared the TS7016 that had tests/scripts/display-name.test.ts quarantined, and it immediately reported a now-unnecessary `@ts-expect-error` in tests/scripts/storybook-retry-report.test.ts which had been suppressing that same missing-declarations error. That directive is deleted and the import is typed.
tagMapIs: The one src/ path in `include`, and it is here so that `document.createElement('kai-…')` in this pass returns the element's real interface instead of a bare HTMLElement. It does NOT put src/ under this pass: element-types.d.ts is a .d.ts and skipLibCheck is on, so nothing in it is CHECKED here — being in the program makes its `declare global` take effect, which is the entire purpose. (The file's own contents are checked by tests/elements/element-types-lib-check.test.ts, which compiles it with skipLibCheck OFF the way a consumer would.) It sits in the CONFIG rather than as an `import type {}` in one test on purpose. The augmentation is global either way, so an import lands it on all ~150 files in the pass regardless of which file wrote it; putting it in one test would make the typing of every other test depend on an import nobody reading them can see. Here it is a property of the pass, stated once. What it bought, measured: it converted the `as HTMLElement & { data: … }` casts in choice/confirm-card/form/tasks-element.test.tsx from assertions that could not fail into four real TS2352, and those four are now gone — see the note in each file about the generated `data` type they were hiding.

structuralExcludes.why: Trees this pass does not own. Unlike a quarantine entry these are not IOUs — nothing here is waiting to be fixed — so verify-quarantine.mjs accepts them without an error expectation. Adding to `exclude` without a line HERE or in `quarantine.entries` fails that check.
structuralExcludes.tests/react: Owned by tsconfig.react.test.json, which compiles it with react-jsx. Checked, just not here.

quarantine.why: Turning this pass on surfaced 36 pre-existing errors in 9 files — exactly what it was built to find. 12 of them were one dead file (tests/animated-logo.tsx), now deleted. The rest were quarantined here rather than papered over with looser compilerOptions, because most needed a src-side fix or a call about intent, not a cast in the test. AN ENTRY HERE IS A DATED IOU, NOT A DECISION: it records the exact errors the file produces, and scripts/verify-quarantine.mjs re-includes the file and asserts it still produces them. Fix the error and that check goes RED until you delete the entry — the list cannot rot closed. Delete an entry and fix the file; do not add entries without a line here saying what broke. THE LIST IS EMPTY as of 2026-08-12 — every IOU below has been paid, and `entries` is kept (rather than deleted) so the next one has an obvious place to go. An empty list does not make the check a no-op: see the note in scripts/verify-quarantine.mjs about what it does instead.

resolved.why: Entries that were quarantined and are now checked by this pass. Kept because what was actually wrong is the useful part, and because a deleted entry teaches nobody anything.
resolved.tests/primitives/card-recovery.test.ts: FIXED — un-quarantined 2026-08-12, in src, which is where the entry said the fix belonged. `dismissRecovery` now returns `Required<Pick<CardPolicy,'onDismiss'|'onReopen'>>`; the bare `Pick` carried CardPolicy's `?` across while the body returned both handlers on every path, so the declaration was strictly weaker than the implementation. The nine TS2722 were therefore all false, and the fix was one word — but NOT test-only noise, which is the part worth keeping: dismissRecovery is exported from src/index.ts and the MCP scaffolder emits `const { onDismiss, onReopen } = dismissRecovery({…})`, so every consumer who destructured and then invoked hit the same error in code we generated for them. This test was just the first caller to do it. The type was tightened onto a measured runtime fact rather than an assumption: card-recovery.test.ts now enumerates the cross-product of the five optional options (32 shapes) and asserts the returned object's own keys are exactly ['onDismiss','onReopen'] and both are callable. Watched in the discriminating direction — making the return conditional on `opts.toast` fails 16 of the 32 — so the `Required` claim is pinned by a test that can see it break.
resolved.tests/remote/host-embed.test.ts: FIXED — un-quarantined 2026-08-12. The entry's own reason was wrong, and worth saying so: 'render-error' was not dropped or renamed, it was never a WireFaultCode in any revision of src/remote/wire.ts (`git log -S "'render-error'" -- '*wire.ts'` is empty; the string appeared nowhere else in the repo). A typo the pass could not see. The test now sends 'render-failed', the code provider-runtime.ts actually posts, and asserts exactly what it did before — the host's fault branch interpolates the code into a message and never validates it, which is why an impossible code passed at runtime for as long as it did.
resolved.tests/scripts/display-name.test.ts: FIXED — un-quarantined 2026-08-12 by `allowJs` (see the note above `include`), which is the option the entry itself proposed first. The .mjs helper is now read and inferred rather than resolved to nothing, so displayNameFromClass arrives typed instead of `any`. The alternative the entry offered — a hand-written .d.mts beside the helper — was rejected on purpose: it would type the import by restating the implementation, and nothing would check the restatement against the .mjs, which is a fresh source of exactly the drift this pass exists to catch.
resolved.tests/stories/element-controls.test.ts: FIXED — un-quarantined 2026-08-12. It was mechanical, as filed: argTypesFor returns Record<string, unknown> and two lines reached inside an entry without narrowing it. Narrowed once, at the point of use, next to the assertions that check the same shape at runtime.
resolved.config/vite/elements.ts (was vite.config: FIXED — un-quarantined 2026-08-12, both by the same one-line change. The entries were right that the type import was broken. Vite imports OutputBundle/OutputChunk from rollup for its own declarations and re-exports them only through its `Rollup` NAMESPACE (`export { rollup as Rollup }`), never as named exports — hence TS2459 and a `chunk` that degraded to unknown, in the generateBundle hook of both minify plugins. Now `import type { Rollup } from 'vite'` with two local aliases, so the existing `as OutputChunk` casts are checked against the real rollup types. Type-only, erased at build time.
resolved.vitest.config.ts: FIXED — un-quarantined 2026-08-12, this pass now checks the file. The TS2769 was load-bearing and the quarantine hid it: `launchOptions` sat inside a browser `instances[]` entry, where @vitest/browser-playwright reads nothing, so the CI chromium hardening never reached the browser. Moved onto the provider (`playwright({ launchOptions })`), which is where the package reads it. That this pass was GREEN on both sides of a real bug is what made the quarantine list self-auditing: see scripts/verify-quarantine.mjs, which now re-includes every quarantined file and fails when one stops producing the error it is excluded for. Verified in the discriminating direction: putting `launchOptions` back on the instance takes this pass from 0 errors to 1x TS2769, which it could not do while the file was excluded.
resolved.tests/components/message.test.tsx: FIXED — un-quarantined, this pass now checks the file. Both errors were real API drift and both were fixed in src/components/message.tsx, not papered over in the test. (1) `<Message role="user">` resolved to the ARIA `role` attribute and was spread onto the row, so the rendered div shipped `role="user"` — measured in a real chromium: the AX tree computed `generic` (the invalid token is discarded, so nothing was mis-announced) and axe reported a CRITICAL `aria-roles` violation, 'Role must be one of the valid ARIA roles: user'. `MessageProps` now Omits ARIA's `role` and declares the SPEAKER union instead; `splitProps` consumes it so it never reaches the DOM, and the row gets `role="article"` + an `aria-label` naming the speaker + `data-role`. The public prop name is unchanged. (2) MessageAvatarProps marked `src`/`alt` required even though the component's whole point is rendering `fallback` when `src` is absent; both are optional now, `alt` defaulting to ''.
resolved.src/elements/resizable.d.ts: FIXED — renamed to src/elements/resizable.globals.d.ts, which puts it in the src pass for the first time. It was unreachable because TypeScript drops a .d.ts when a same-named .ts/.tsx sits beside it, and resizable.tsx does. The rename makes the HTMLElementEventMap half work (measured: `el.addEventListener('kai-maximize-intent', e => e.detail)` was TS2339 before and narrows correctly after). The HTMLElementTagNameMap half is now fixed too, but in the GENERATOR, not here: the hand-written interface could never win against element-types.d.ts's same-named one, so resizable.tsx routes maximize/restore through `ctx.expose` and gen-element-types.mjs emits every exposed method onto the element interface (tests/elements/element-methods-typed.test.ts). Note also that no pass CHECKS a .d.ts body: every one sets skipLibCheck, so being in the program makes the augmentation take effect, not get verified — which is why that guard compiles the file itself.

nowCovered.the generated HTMLElementTagNameMap: WAS in notAlsoCovered, DONE 2026-08-12. The gap was that this pass had no `src/**`, so element-types.d.ts was not in the program, every `document.createElement('kai-…')` was a plain HTMLElement, and the `as HTMLElement & { data: … }` casts in choice/confirm-card/form/tasks-element.test.tsx widened a type that was already HTMLElement. How dead those casts were, measured rather than argued: the IDENTICAL cast compiled against 'kai-confirm' and against 'kai-not-a-real-element', and errored only for 'div' — the one tag tsc actually knew. The map is now in `include` (see "tagMapIs"), the four casts are gone, and createElement returns the real element interface. The four were NOT load-bearing as assertions and they WERE hiding something: with the map present, `el.data = someCardInterface` is TS2322, because gen-element-types.mjs emits `data?: Record<string, unknown>` and no exported card interface is assignable to that — interfaces get no implicit index signature. That is a live consumer bug, not test noise: each element's own doc comment tells consumers to import the payload type ("Import `ChoiceCardData` from `@kitn.ai/ui` for the full shape") and the declared prop then rejects it. The fix belongs in the GENERATOR and is filed for whoever owns it; each of the four marks the line with `@ts-expect-error` meanwhile, so the day `data` is typed properly all four go TS2578 and have to be revisited. Unchanged: the elements' interaction METHODS were never affected — element-methods-typed.test.ts compiles the shipped declarations directly, the way a consumer does.

notAlsoCovered..storybook/**: Left out on purpose. .storybook/preview.ts imports ../dist/kai.es.js — a gitignored build artifact — so the file cannot typecheck before a build, and `nx typecheck ui` must not require one. (For the record, a probe over the three files reports 2 errors: that missing-module import, plus API_HashEntry.title in manager.ts.)
